stem.text: The molecules of a gas at a constant temperature, $T_1$, have the distribution of molecular energies shown in the diagram.

stem.alt: Graph of proportion of molecules with a given energy against molecular energy, showing one curve labelled T1 that rises to a peak and then falls.
stem.label: T1

stem.text: When the temperature is **increased** to $T_2$, the distribution of molecular energies changes.
Which diagram correctly shows this change?

A.alt: Graph with T1 solid curve and T2 dashed curve; T2 peaks higher and at lower molecular energy than T1, and the curves cross.

B.alt: Graph with T1 solid curve and T2 dashed curve; T2 lies above T1 at all energies, peaking at the same energy as T1 but higher.

C.alt: Graph with T1 solid curve and T2 dashed curve; T2 peaks at a higher molecular energy and greater height than T1, and the curves cross.

D.alt: Graph with T1 solid curve and T2 dashed curve; T2 peaks at a higher molecular energy and lower height than T1, and the curves cross.
